newsitem.title: GERMANY: Rexrodt says Germany has good chance on EMU goal.
newsitem.headline: Rexrodt says Germany has good chance on EMU goal.

text.p: Germany has good chances of fulfilling the EMU deficit goal this year, and will make extra efforts if it appears the target could be missed, Economics Minister Guenther Rexrodt said on Monday.
"We have good chances of filling the deficit criterion," Rexrodt said at a panel discussion at the Hanover Industry Trade Fair. "If we do not fill it, we must make renewed efforts."

Rexrodt repeated Bonn's forecast that economic growth should rebound to 2.5 percent this year, boosting tax revenues and improving Germany's chances of narrowing its budget deficit to three percent of economic output.
That is one of the goals set by the Maastricht Treaty for countries seeking to participate in EMU.

Lower Saxony Premier Gerhardt Schroeder, a potential candidate for chancellor from the opposition Social Democrats, said Germany should seek a delay in the scheduled January 1999 start of EMU, if it fails to meet the criteria.
"If Germany cannot meet the criteria, we should discuss the timetable," Schroeder said.
Bavarian Premier Edmund Stoiber said Germany had no political leeway for anything other than a strict interpretation of the three percent Maastricht deficit target.
Rexrodt said in extracts from a statement he was due to deliver: "We can and will achieve the Maastricht criteria, and thus ensure that Europe does not miss this historic chance."
